guards.what: EnjoyTea (RoundTeaParty.cs:40-46): RelicCmd.Obtain<RoyalPoison> FIRST, then Heal(MaxHp - CurrentHp) with both read AFTER the obtain
guards.maps_to: events/round_tea_party.py:39-42 add_relic('royal_poison') then `run.heal(run.max_hp - run.hp)`, reading both after the grant, which is what the source does -- it captures the Creature reference before the obtain but evaluates MaxHp/CurrentHp inside the Heal call (RoundTeaParty.cs:42-44). The order is only observable for a relic that moves max HP on pickup, and Royal Poison does not (relics/royal_poison.py has no after_obtained, only a turn-1 AfterPlayerTurnStart chip) -- but the sim preserves it anyway. This is a plain CreatureCmd.Heal, which dispatches no hooks in C# either (CreatureCmd.cs:691-703), so turn_structure step 38a does NOT apply -- confirmed by `py audit/tools/event_probes.py heal`, which lists this event under the plain-heal verb.

guards.what: EV-1: ContinueFight's 11 HP loss (RoundTeaParty.cs:56) can reduce the player to 0 HP. C# routes event damage through CreatureCmd.Damage, whose Hook.ShouldDie / Hook.AfterPreventingDeath pass runs over RunState.IterateHookListeners (RunState.cs:545-596), which yields the POTION BELT outside combat; RunState.lose_hp (run.py:420-432, was :294-302) just subtracts
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): the run-level death pass is complete. `RunState.lose_hp` already clamped at 0 (Creature.LoseHpInternal, Creature.cs:450) and already ran `_resolve_death` -- CreatureCmd's Kill tail (CreatureCmd.cs:504-570) over the belt, which is the only limb of RunState.IterateHookListeners (RunState.cs:545-596) carrying a ported death listener. What was left was the LAST line of this entry's own fix note: Fairy in a Bottle's `after_preventing_death` opened with `if self.combat is None: return`, so the preventer was found and then did nothing. That early return is now the OUT-OF-COMBAT ARM of OnUseWrapper instead -- RemoveBeforeUse nulls the belt slot and the new `FairyInABottle.use_out_of_combat` heals -- which is what PotionModel.cs:294/:298/:334/:336/:340's null-combat guards reduce the wrapper to, and the same reading RunState.use_potion already recorded. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/event_probes.py lethal` -- all three legs MATCH (alive, hp 24, Fairy consumed) where all three read DIVERGE. test/test_events.py::TestRunLevelDeathPrevention pins both outcomes, including the no-Fairy run ending dead at exactly 0.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-28 -- STILL A GAP. Two legs closed, the decisive one did not. CLOSED: RunState.lose_hp (run.py:420-432, was :304-316) now clamps at 0 (no more negative HP) and runs the run-level death-prevention pass -- `_resolve_death` (run.py:434-461, was :318-345) walks the potion belt asking `should_die` and calls `after_preventing_death` on the preventer, the port of CreatureCmd.KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition (CreatureCmd.cs:489-571). REMAINS: the belt Fairy's out-of-combat arm. FairyInABottle.should_die (potions.py:1394, was :1310-1311) answers False so the Fairy IS selected as the preventer, but FairyInABottle.after_preventing_death (potions.py:1397, was :1313-1316) still returns immediately when `self.combat is None`, so nothing heals, `_resolve_death` re-kills through its 10 recursions, and the player still ends DEAD with the Fairy still in the belt. EXECUTED 2026-07-28 (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py lethal`, plus ad-hoc at the repo root): 5 HP + belt Fairy, lose 15 -> sim hp=0, dead, belt still ['FairyInABottle']; the game ends alive at 24 HP with the Fairy consumed. LIVE exactly as before -- only the negative-HP secondary is fixed.

guards.what: `runState.Players.All(...)` (RoundTeaParty.cs:28), the Royal Poison hover tip and the `.ThatDoesDamage(11)` annotation (RoundTeaParty.cs:35-36)
guards.rationale: multiplayer-only: the C# predicate is `runState.Players.All(p => ...)`, a quantifier over the party. The sim is single-player, so the quantifier collapses to the one player's clause, which the sim implements exactly. Out of scope per the shared contract's multiplayer waiver.

EventOption.ThatWontSaveToChoiceHistory (EventOption.cs:220) marks the option out of the run's MapPointHistory choice log. The sim has no choice-history subsystem at all, so there is nothing for the flag to switch off, and grep shows only three call sites in the whole source (RoundTeaParty.cs:50 and TheArchitect.cs:334, 339) -- all of them second-page 'continue' buttons, i.e. the flag exists so a history replay does not record a non-choice. Same observable game state; recorded as a divergence rather than a waiver because run history is not one of the contract's four out-of-scope categories, and a future history/telemetry port would need it. Same treatment as GoldLossType.Stolen on the morphic_grove record.
